cards.text: Jeroboam, king of Israel, has set up a golden calf and his own altar in Bethel (1 Kings 12:29, 33). He's standing beside that altar to burn incense when, suddenly, a man of God from Judah shows up by the word of the LORD. And friend, this man did NOT come to sit quietly in the back row.

cards.question: The man of God cries out by the word of the LORD. He cries out against the ___.

cards.text: He yells, "O altar, O altar," and gives it a message from the LORD. Friend, he is preaching to the FURNITURE.

The LORD's message: a son named Josiah will be born to the house of David. On this very altar he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense on it, and human bones will be burned on it.

cards.question: That same day, the man of God gives a sign from the LORD. What does the sign say will happen?

cards.text: King Jeroboam hears every word. He stretches out his hand toward the man of God and says, "Seize him!"

cards.question: Jeroboam's hand is stretched out toward the man of God. What happens to the king's hand?

cards.text: And the altar splits apart, and the ashes pour out, just like the sign said. Friend, when this man of God gives a sign, you can set your oven timer by it.

cards.question: With his hand stuck, Jeroboam asks the man of God to ___ for him.

cards.text: The man of God prays to the LORD, and the king's hand is restored, just like before. One minute it's seize him, next minute it's please pray for me, and friend, that is a FAST change of tune.

cards.question: Now the king invites the man of God home to refresh himself and offers him a reward. True or false: the man of God accepts.

cards.text: He says even if the king gave him half his possessions, he still wouldn't go with him, or eat bread or drink water in this place. Friend, I can't walk past a free cookie sample, and this man just walked past HALF of everything a king owns.

cards.question: Why won't the man of God eat bread or drink water in Bethel?

answers.text: The LORD commanded him not to
He doesn't trust the king's food
He wants to get home before dark

cards.question: The LORD's command also covered the man of God's trip home. How does he leave Bethel?

answers.text: He goes back the way he came
He waits for the king's escort

cards.text: Now an old prophet lives in Bethel. His sons come home and tell him everything the man of God did that day, and what he said to the king.

cards.question: The old prophet hears all about the man of God from Judah, who has already left Bethel. What does he ask his sons?

cards.text: He says, "Saddle the donkey for me," and off he rides after him. This man hears ONE story and he's out the door, like me when somebody says a fresh batch just came out of the oven.
He finds the man of God sitting under an oak tree and checks that he's the one from Judah. Then the old prophet says, "Come home with me and eat some bread."

cards.question: The old prophet invites him home to eat some bread. True or false: the man of God says yes.

cards.text: He tells the old prophet what the LORD commanded him. Then the old prophet says he's a prophet too, and an angel told him by the word of the LORD to bring the man back for bread and water.

cards.question: The LORD gave the man of God his orders by His own word. Now the old prophet claims an angel brought different orders. True or false: the old prophet is lying.
The man of God hears the old prophet's claim about the angel. What does he do?

answers.text: Goes back and eats at his house
Asks the LORD to confirm it first

cards.question: While the man of God and the old prophet are sitting at the table, the word of the LORD comes. Who does it come to?
The old prophet cries out the LORD's message to the man of God: he has ___ the word of the LORD.

cards.text: Because the man of God went back and ate bread and drank water where the LORD told him not to, the LORD says his body will never reach the tomb of his fathers.

After the meal, the old prophet saddles the donkey for him, and the man of God heads out. On the road, a lion meets him and kills him, and his body is left lying there with the donkey and the lion standing beside it.

cards.question: Men passing by see the man of God's body in the road with the lion beside it. What do they do?

answers.text: Report it in the old prophet's city
Bury the body by the roadside
Carry the body back to Judah

cards.question: True or false: when the old prophet hears the news, he says the lion found the man of God by chance.

cards.text: The old prophet's sons saddle the donkey for him again, and he rides out and finds the body in the road.

cards.question: True or false: the lion has not eaten the body or mauled the donkey.
The old prophet lifts the body onto the donkey. What does he do with it?

answers.text: Lays it in his own tomb

cards.text: They lament over him, crying, "Oh, my brother!"

cards.question: The old prophet tells his sons that when he dies, they must lay his ___ beside the man of God's.
Why does the old prophet want to be buried beside the man of God?

answers.text: The man's message will surely come true
The man had asked to be buried with him
The king had commanded it for prophets

cards.text: And Jeroboam? Withered hand, split altar, and he STILL doesn't turn from his evil ways. Friend, the ALTAR cracked before the king did.

cards.question: Instead of repenting, what does Jeroboam do again?

answers.text: Makes anyone who wants it a priest
Builds a brand new altar in Dan
Sets up a third golden calf

cards.question: Jeroboam keeps making priests for the high places. True or false: the passage says this sin of his house leads to its destruction from the face of the earth.

cards.text: We'll let the ovens cool on that one for now. But hold on to your apron, friend, because this kingdom's story is not done yet.
